If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for late horizon (days 20–30) to correct for sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon (days 20–30) to reflect sustained momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for late horizon (days 20–30) to reflect weakening momentum.

If sentiment is positive but forecast is overestimating (model > true by >2% for 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (days 1–5) to correct for sentiment-driven overconfidence.
